name: slow credential guessing from a foreign host
rationale: The shipped burst detector keys on four failures inside ten minutes. Variants using slow_guess spread the same ten failures over eighteen hours and walk straight past it. Counting failures per day instead of per burst keeps the signal and loses the timing assumption.
explain: {user} failed to log in {count} times in 24 hours from {ip}, which belongs to {ip_owner}.

name: csrf payload in a forum parameter
rationale: The real payloads literally contain payload=csrf_test and action=csrf_role_update, so a substring match on csrf catches the March incident perfectly. It catches nothing else, because the attacker chose those words and an attacker who renames the parameter picks different ones.
explain: {user} sent a forum parameter containing csrf from {ip}.

parse.grammar_note: CONTAINS and the query field are not in the section 10 grammar, whose field list is user|ip|ip_owner|template|obj_id|status|signal. C either extends the grammar or this rule is rejected at parse time rather than at the gate.

gate.rejected_reason: Held-out detection 0.00 against a threshold of 0.60. The rule matches the one string the attacker happened to use. Every param_rename variant renames that parameter, so the rule detects the incident it was written from and nothing else. That is memorisation, not detection.
